idiom_name: Playwright TS: class with readonly Locator fields and typed async methods
implementation_notes: The TypeScript form of the Playwright POM is a class with readonly Locator fields created from the constructor's Page parameter, async methods whose signatures document the flow, and imports of the framework's own types (import type { Locator, Page } from '@playwright/test'). Types replace reflection: locators are typed values rather than strings at call sites, navigation methods can return the next page class so a changed flow is a compile error, and auto-waiting locators mean no explicit sleeps while expect() stays in the test. Choose it for Playwright suites; the WebdriverIO variant otherwise.
pitfalls: Locators are lazy, element handles are not: storing await page.$() results in typed fields still compiles and still goes stale.
Creating every locator in the constructor couples the class to the initial page; locators that only exist after navigation belong in the method that navigates (or in lazy getters).
Strict null checks expose optional chaining in page methods; silencing it with non-null assertions hides genuine absent-element states.

variants.name: WebdriverIO typed page objects: exported instance with lazy typed getters
variants.idiom_name: WebdriverIO typed page with lazy getters and an exported singleton
variants.implementation_notes: WebdriverIO's TypeScript setup makes the getter style first-class: the page class exposes elements as getters (get username() { return $('#username') }), exports a single instance, and types flow from the registered framework globals, so chaining reads as await LoginPage.username.setValue('max') and a renamed getter fails to compile. The getter keeps the element command lazy, and custom commands can be declared on the framework's types so call sites stay checked. Choose it for WebdriverIO suites; the Playwright variant otherwise.
pitfalls: A getter returns the framework's element command, not a resolved element: awaiting it eagerly or destructuring it defeats the lazy command and can pin the previous document.
The singleton export is safe only while page objects stay stateless; mutable state on the singleton leaks across spec files.

Custom commands are global at runtime but checked only through the declared framework types; keep the declaration and the registration in sync or call sites compile against commands that do not exist.
